md_name: Marine microbial sequencing and environmental metadata workflow
md_description: This workflow covers collection of marine microbial samples from diverse ocean regions, preparation of sequencing libraries, generation of genomic sequencing reads, and computational derivation of microbial diversity summaries. It is designed to connect microbial composition results with environmental context including geographic coordinates, depth, temperature, biome type, and proximity to features such as hydrothermal vents.

marine_water_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin metadata for the collected marine sample: site coordinates, collection depth, collection temperature, biome, and local environmental feature context. I excluded downstream process details (preservation, extraction, library prep), capture/instrument settings, and all signal/derivative properties because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any sample or experiment identifiers since none were already generated here and those are typically root-level identifiers, not repeated on this entity. The field set is limited to the minimum collection-context descriptors needed to interpret and reuse the sample in environmental analyses.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the marine water sample at collection time, used to link all downstream data products to this source sample. Example format: MWS-000123.
Identifier for the oceanic sampling site or station where the sample was collected. Example format: SITE-ARCTIC-05.
Geographic latitude of the sampling location recorded at collection time, in decimal degrees (typical range -90 to 90). Positive values indicate north; negative values indicate south.
Geographic longitude of the sampling location recorded at collection time, in decimal degrees (typical range -180 to 180). Positive values indicate east; negative values indicate west.
Water depth at which the marine sample was collected, measured at the sampling point in meters below sea surface (typical range 0 to several thousand meters).
Water temperature at the time and place of sample collection, measured in degrees Celsius at the sampling point (typical marine range about -2 to 35).
Broad marine biome classification for the sampling site as recorded during collection, used to contextualize microbial diversity analyses.

Specific nearby environmental feature or habitat attribute noted at the sampling site at collection time, such as proximity to hydrothermal vents, reef structures, or other localized oceanographic features.

Material collected for sequencing at the source site, indicating whether the sample was seawater, particulate matter, or a mixed marine microbial fraction. Record the collection material category used for this sample.

sample_preservation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only preservation-operation metadata: how the collected marine sample was stabilized for downstream molecular work, including the preservation approach, temperature, duration, and any fixative or storage medium used. I also added a process quality/stability indicator because that describes the operation outcome, not the resulting preserved sample itself. I excluded intrinsic sample descriptors like latitude, depth, biome, and sample identifiers because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I avoided downstream preserved-sample properties, which belong to the preserved_marine_sample Entity.

md_schema.descr: Method used to stabilize the collected marine sample immediately after collection for downstream nucleic-acid workflows. Record the preservation approach applied in this experiment, such as freezing, chemical fixation, or filtration-based storage.

Temperature used during sample preservation and short-term stabilization, measured at the time of preservation in degrees Celsius. Typical values may range from about -80 to 20 depending on the preservation method.

Elapsed time from sample collection to completion of preservation handling, measured in minutes. Use the total time window during which the sample remained under preservation-relevant handling conditions.
Chemical or physical medium used to preserve the marine sample, if applicable. Examples include RNAlater, ethanol, sterile buffer, or no added medium for direct freezing.
Operational assessment of whether the sample preservation step met the workflow's handling criteria for downstream molecular processing, recorded after preservation was completed.

preserved_marine_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only the preserved sample's intrinsic state and storage-ready identity, not the preservation protocol itself or downstream extraction/library steps. The fields describe what the preserved sample is and its condition after preservation: preservation status, storage form, storage temperature, storage duration, and container/aliquot context. I excluded collection-site environmental metadata because those belong to the original marine_water_sample Entity, and I avoided repeating preservation method details already owned by the sample_preservation Process.

md_schema.descr: Current status of the marine sample after the preservation process, indicating that it is ready for nucleic acid extraction and library preparation. Record the status at the time the preserved sample is accessioned or transferred.

Physical form in which the preserved sample is held after stabilization, such as frozen whole sample, pellet, or buffered liquid aliquot. Record the form present when the sample is moved into storage or downstream processing.

Temperature at which the preserved marine sample is stored after preservation and before DNA extraction, measured in degrees Celsius. Typical storage values may include -80, -20, 4, or ambient depending on workflow.
Duration for which the sample remained in preserved storage before nucleic acid extraction, measured in days. Record the total storage time from preservation completion to extraction start.
Container or vessel used to hold the preserved sample during storage, such as cryovial, tube, or filter cartridge. Record the container type present before extraction.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only DNA extraction operation details: extraction chemistry, kit or protocol, elution volume, yield, and a process-level purity/quality indicator. I excluded preserved-sample storage attributes and all downstream extracted-DNA properties because those belong to the input Entity and output Entity nodes, respectively. I also avoided repeating any sample identity or collection context, since those are outside the semantic territory of the extraction process.

md_schema.descr: Name of the DNA extraction kit or protocol used on the preserved marine sample. Record the exact kit or method applied at the extraction step, for example a commercial marine DNA kit or a custom phenol-chloroform workflow.
Version, lot-specific protocol revision, or vendor release associated with the extraction kit or method used for DNA isolation. Record only if the workflow distinguishes between versions.
Cell lysis approach used during extraction to release nucleic acids from the preserved marine microbial material. Examples include bead beating, enzymatic lysis, chemical lysis, or a combined method.
Final elution volume used to recover extracted DNA from the extraction workflow, measured in microliters at the completion of the process. Typical values may range from 20 to 200 microliters.

Amount of DNA recovered from the extraction process, measured at the end of extraction in nanograms using the assay specified by the laboratory. Typical values vary widely with marine biomass and sample volume.
Operational assessment of extracted DNA suitability for library preparation, recorded after extraction based on contamination, integrity, and quantity checks.

extracted_marine_dna.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the extracted DNA fraction: concentration, total yield, purity ratios, fragment integrity, and storage state. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream dna_extraction Process, and I excluded library-prep parameters because those belong downstream. I also avoided sample collection metadata and sample identifiers already handled at the root sample entity. The fields chosen are the minimum needed to assess whether the DNA is suitable for library construction.

md_schema.descr: Measured concentration of the extracted marine DNA fraction at the time it is accessioned for library preparation, in nanograms per microliter. Record the concentration from the assay used immediately after extraction or after normalization if that is the value transferred forward.
Total amount of DNA recovered in the extracted fraction, measured at the point the DNA is handed off to library preparation. Typical values depend on biomass and extraction efficiency.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio (A260/A280) for the extracted DNA fraction, measured after extraction and before library preparation. Typical values for relatively pure DNA are around 1.8.
Assessment of whether the extracted DNA fraction is sufficiently intact for sequencing library construction, recorded after extraction quality control.
Storage condition of the extracted DNA fraction before library preparation, such as frozen, refrigerated, or immediate-use. Record the condition at the time the DNA is transferred to the next step.

library_preparation.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only library-preparation operation metadata: the protocol/kit used, indexing strategy, insert size target, amplification parameters, input DNA amount, and a library-quality outcome indicator. I excluded intrinsic DNA properties because those belong to the extracted_marine_dna Entity, and I did not include raw-read or sequencing instrument settings because those belong downstream to the capture and signal nodes. I also avoided duplicating process-agent software/hardware details not relevant here, since this node is a wet-lab process run by a technician rather than a software process.

md_schema.descr: Name of the library preparation kit or protocol used to convert extracted marine DNA into sequencing-ready libraries. Record the exact kit or validated protocol applied in this step.
Version, lot, or protocol revision for the library preparation kit or workflow used at this step, if tracked by the laboratory.
Indexing or barcode strategy used to multiplex the library for sequencing. Record whether single indexing, dual indexing, or another strategy was used.
Target insert size produced by the library preparation workflow, measured in base pairs and defined at the end of library construction. Typical values depend on sequencing platform and protocol.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library preparation, recorded during or immediately after library construction. Use the total cycle count applied to this sample.
Amount of extracted marine DNA input into library preparation, measured in nanograms at the start of the process. Typical values depend on kit requirements and sample yield.
Operational assessment of whether the prepared library met internal quality criteria for sequencing, recorded after library QC and before sequencing.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared library itself: library identifier, concentration, fragment size profile, indexing/barcode identity, molarity, and storage condition. I excluded preparation protocol details because those belong to the upstream library_preparation Process, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings and raw file properties because those belong downstream to genomic_sequencing and raw_fastq_reads. The selected fields are the minimal library descriptors needed to understand what material entered sequencing and how it was tracked and reused.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library accessioned from the library preparation step. Example format: LIB-000123.
Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library at the time it is sent to sequencing, in nanograms per microliter. Record the concentration from the final library QC measurement.
Calculated molarity of the prepared sequencing library at the time of sequencing setup, measured in nanomolar units. Use the value used for pooling or loading if applicable.

Observed or expected average insert size of the sequencing library, measured in base pairs after library QC and before sequencing. Typical values depend on the library prep protocol and sequencing platform.
Barcode or index sequence associated with the prepared library for sample multiplexing. Record the actual index sequence used for this library.

Storage condition of the prepared sequencing library before it is loaded onto the sequencing instrument, such as frozen, refrigerated, or immediate-use. Record the condition at the time of sequencing handoff.

genomic_sequencing.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only instrument/session configuration and actively controlled sequencing settings: platform identity, run identifiers, flow cell/run mode, read length, lane/indexing/loading parameters, and sequencing quality metrics. I also included hardware agent properties (manufacturer, model, serial number) as required for capture nodes. I excluded sample-origin fields like coordinates, depth, temperature, and biome because those belong to the source Entity, not the capture session. I also excluded file format and file-location details because those belong to the downstream raw_fastq_reads Signal.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session. Record the hardware vendor of the platform that generated the raw marine microbial reads.
Model name or platform designation of the sequencing instrument used for genomic sequencing, recorded for the capture session. Example: NovaSeq 6000.
Serial number or unique hardware identifier for the sequencing instrument used in this capture session. Record the instrument serial as printed by the manufacturer or instrument inventory system.
Unique identifier for the sequencing run/session in which the marine library was read. Example format: RUN-2024-00045.
Flow cell or sequencing cartridge type loaded for this capture session, recorded at run setup. Use the platform-specific flow cell designation.
Configured read length per sequencing cycle for this run, measured in base pairs and set at run initialization. Typical values depend on platform and chemistry, such as 2x150 bp.
Whether the capture session was configured to generate paired-end reads or single-end reads, recorded at sequencing run setup.
Lane or comparable physical partition used for this sequencing run, if applicable to the platform. Record the lane assignment used during capture.

Target number of read pairs or reads planned for this capture session, measured in millions of reads and set before or during run setup. Typical values depend on desired coverage and multiplexing design.

Operational quality indicator for the sequencing capture session, recorded after the run completes but before raw-file interpretation. Examples include run pass/fail or instrument-level yield/quality assessment.

raw_fastq_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artifact descriptors: file format, file size, read count, read structure, base quality summaries, and storage location. I excluded capture settings like sequencer model and read length because those belong to the upstream genomic_sequencing Capture, and I excluded QC or biological interpretation because those belong to downstream processes or derivatives. The fields are limited to technical properties needed to locate, validate, and reuse the raw FASTQ artifacts.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw sequencing read artifact produced by the genomic sequencing capture step. Record the technical format of the raw reads, typically FASTQ or gzipped FASTQ.
Total size of the raw FASTQ read file(s) at the time of storage, measured in bytes. Record the on-disk size of the raw artifact produced by sequencing.
Total number of reads or read pairs contained in the raw FASTQ artifact, counted from the file content after sequencing completion. Use the count corresponding to the stored raw data object.
Average length of reads in the raw FASTQ artifact, measured in base pairs and calculated from the stored sequencing file. Typical values reflect the instrument configuration used upstream.
Average per-base quality score across the raw FASTQ reads, computed from the file contents as a technical quality summary of the raw artifact.
Storage location or URI for the raw FASTQ file artifact produced by sequencing, such as a local path, object-store URI, or repository link.
Whether the raw FASTQ artifact is stored compressed or uncompressed at rest, recorded for the file as stored. Use this to distinguish gzipped files from plain text files.

read_qc_and_trimming.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only read-processing operation metadata: the trimming/QC tool and version, adapter handling, quality thresholds, minimum length, and a process-level pass/warning/fail outcome. I excluded raw-read file properties because those belong to the input Signal, and I excluded clean-read artifact properties because those belong to the downstream Signal. I also avoided capture settings and biological interpretation because they are outside the semantic scope of this computational processing step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software tool used to quality-filter and trim the raw marine sequencing reads. Record the exact program applied in this step, for example fastp or a comparable read-processing tool.
Version of the QC/trimming software used on the raw FASTQ reads, recorded for reproducibility of the processing step.
Adapter sequence reference or adapter set used during trimming, recorded at the time of processing. Use the adapter kit name, sequence reference, or preset used by the tool.
Per-base quality score threshold applied during trimming/filtering, measured on the Phred scale. Record the cutoff used to remove low-quality bases or reads.
Minimum read length retained after trimming, measured in base pairs. Reads shorter than this threshold are discarded during processing.
Fraction of raw reads retained after QC and trimming, calculated as retained reads divided by input reads for this process step. Record the value immediately after processing completes.
Operational assessment of whether the trimming/QC step produced reads suitable for downstream taxonomic profiling, recorded at the end of processing.

clean_fastq_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only technical properties of the cleaned read artifact: file format, file size, retained read count, post-QC length summary, post-QC quality summary, storage location, and compression status. I excluded trimming parameters and software details because those belong to the upstream read_qc_and_trimming Process, and I excluded downstream analysis outputs because those belong to later Process/Derivative nodes. The field set is the minimum needed to identify and reuse the cleaned FASTQ artifact.

md_schema.descr: File format of the quality-filtered read artifact retained after trimming and filtering. Record the technical format of the cleaned reads, typically FASTQ or gzipped FASTQ.
Total size of the cleaned FASTQ file(s) at the time of storage, measured in bytes. Record the on-disk size of the post-QC read artifact.
Total number of reads or read pairs retained after QC and trimming, counted from the cleaned FASTQ artifact. Use the count corresponding to the stored cleaned data object.
Average length of reads in the cleaned FASTQ artifact, measured in base pairs and calculated from the post-QC file contents. Typical values reflect trimming and filtering effects.
Average per-base quality score across the cleaned reads, computed from the post-QC FASTQ artifact as a technical quality summary.
Storage location or URI for the cleaned FASTQ artifact used for downstream analysis, such as a local path, object-store URI, or repository link.
Whether the cleaned FASTQ artifact is stored compressed or uncompressed at rest, recorded for the file as stored.

taxonomic_profiling.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only computational profiling operation metadata: the profiling tool, version, database/reference, key classification thresholds, abundance normalization choice, and a process-level result quality flag. I excluded clean-read file properties because those belong to the input Signal, and I excluded the abundance table itself because that belongs to the downstream taxa_abundance_profile Derivative. I also included the software agent property because process nodes own software identity per the workflow rules.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software tool used to assign clean marine reads to microbial taxa. Record the exact program applied in this step, for example Kraken2 or a comparable classifier.
Version of the taxonomic profiling software used on the cleaned reads, recorded for reproducibility of the computational step.
Name of the reference database or taxonomy database used by the profiling tool. Record the exact database release or curated reference set applied during classification.
Version, release date, or build identifier for the reference database used in taxonomic profiling, if tracked by the workflow.

Minimum confidence or score threshold required for a taxonomic assignment to be accepted, recorded as used in this profiling step. The scale depends on the classifier and should match the tool's parameterization.

Method used to normalize taxonomic counts into abundances during profiling, recorded at the end of the computational assignment step. Examples include raw counts, relative abundance, or copy-number adjusted abundance.
Operational assessment of whether the taxonomic profiling output is suitable for downstream abundance-table generation and diversity analysis, recorded after classification completes.

taxa_abundance_profile.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result metadata: the abundance table format, dimensions, taxonomic rank, normalization/aggregation method, sparsity, and a computed quality/completeness indicator. I excluded profiling tool parameters because those belong to the upstream taxonomic_profiling Process, and I excluded downstream diversity metrics and modeling fields because those belong to later Derivative and Process nodes. The selected fields describe the derived community-composition table itself and how it was computed, without repeating raw signal properties.

md_schema.descr: File or table format of the computed taxa abundance profile produced from taxonomic profiling. Record the stored representation used for downstream analysis, such as TSV, CSV, or parquet.
Number of rows in the taxa abundance profile table at the time it is finalized, corresponding to taxa entries or sample-taxon records depending on table layout.
Number of columns in the taxa abundance profile table at the time it is finalized, corresponding to samples, taxa metadata, or abundance measures depending on layout.
Taxonomic rank represented in the abundance profile, recorded for the derived table after profiling. Examples include species, genus, family, or higher ranks depending on classifier output.

Normalization or scaling method used to represent abundances in the derived table, recorded when the abundance profile is computed. Examples include raw counts, relative abundance, or transformed abundance values.
Fraction of zero or empty abundance entries in the derived table, calculated from the final taxa abundance profile as a summary of table sparsity. Typical values range from 0 to 1.
Computed assessment of completeness and consistency of the taxa abundance table, recorded after table generation and before downstream diversity analysis.

alpha_diversity_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computation settings and summary outputs of the alpha-diversity calculation: the software/tool and version, the specific diversity indices computed, any rarefaction or sampling depth setting, and a process-level quality flag. I excluded the input abundance-table properties because those belong to the upstream taxa_abundance_profile Derivative, and I excluded the resulting metric values because those belong to the downstream diversity_metrics Derivative. I also avoided environmental covariates and modeling fields because those are reserved for the later association-modeling step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analytical tool used to compute within-sample alpha diversity metrics from the taxa abundance profiles. Record the exact program applied in this step, for example QIIME 2 or a similar diversity-analysis tool.
Version of the diversity-analysis software used to compute alpha diversity metrics, recorded for reproducibility of the computational step.
Set of alpha diversity indices computed during this analysis step. Record the indices calculated from the taxa abundance profiles, such as richness, Shannon, or Simpson.

Rarefaction depth or sampling depth used before computing alpha diversity, measured as the number of sequences per sample. Record the exact depth applied in this analysis step if rarefaction was used.
Minimum sample coverage or completeness threshold required for inclusion in the alpha diversity calculation, recorded if the analysis filtered samples by coverage before computing metrics.
Operational assessment of whether the alpha diversity computation completed successfully and produced metrics suitable for downstream comparison and modeling.

diversity_metrics.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only the computed alpha-diversity results and their derived quality descriptors: metric values, metric names, units, sample count, and a completeness/quality flag. I excluded the software and rarefaction settings because those belong to the upstream alpha_diversity_analysis Process, and I excluded environmental covariates and modeling outputs because those belong downstream to the association-modeling derivative. The fields focus on the final diversity summary table itself and its immediate interpretability.

md_schema.descr: Name of the alpha diversity metric stored in the derived diversity table for each sample. Examples include observed_richness, shannon_index, or simpson_index.
Numeric value of the alpha diversity metric computed for a sample, recorded in the final derived output. The scale and typical range depend on the chosen metric.
Units associated with the diversity metric value, if applicable. Some alpha diversity metrics are unitless, while others may be expressed as counts or indices.
Number of marine samples included in the final diversity metrics output, recorded for the derived result table. Use this as a summary of the computation scope.
Assessment of whether the computed diversity metrics are complete and suitable for comparison across samples, recorded after metric generation.

environmental_association_modeling.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only modeling-operation metadata: the statistical software and version, model type, response and predictor specification, random-effects structure, fit/selection criterion, and a model-quality flag. I excluded environmental source fields like latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, and biome because those belong to the upstream sample entity and are inputs to the model rather than process settings. I also excluded the final coefficients, p-values, and predictions because those belong to the downstream association-results derivative.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical software or package used to fit the environmental association model. Record the exact tool applied in this step, for example R or an R package workflow.
Version of the statistical software or package used for the environmental association model, recorded for reproducibility of the process.
Statistical model class used to relate diversity metrics to environmental variables. Record the fitted model family or structure used in this step.
Name of the diversity metric used as the model response variable, recorded at model setup. Example values include Shannon index or observed richness.

Set of environmental predictors included in the fitted model, recorded as the variables used in the analysis step. Examples include latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, biome type, and hydrothermal vent proximity.
Random-effects structure included in the association model, if any, such as sample site or region grouping. Record the grouping term specified at model fit time.
Criterion used to evaluate or compare candidate models in this step, such as AIC, BIC, or cross-validation score, recorded after model fitting.
Operational assessment of whether the fitted environmental association model converged and produced interpretable results suitable for downstream reporting.

env_diversity_association_results.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only the computed association-result fields: effect estimates, uncertainty, significance, adjusted significance, model fit summary, and a result-quality flag. I excluded the modeling software and predictor specification because those belong to the upstream environmental_association_modeling Process, and I excluded source environmental variables because those belong to the sample Entity. The fields are limited to the statistical outputs needed to interpret and reuse the modeled relationships between diversity and environment.

md_schema.descr: Name of the environmental term or predictor reported in the association results table, such as latitude, longitude, depth, temperature, biome type, or hydrothermal vent proximity.

Estimated effect size for the association between the diversity metric and the environmental term, reported from the fitted model. Use the numeric coefficient or comparable effect estimate from the final results table.
Unit or scale associated with the effect size estimate, if applicable. For standardized coefficients this may be unitless; otherwise record the predictor scale used in the model.
Standard error of the effect size estimate for the association result, reported from the fitted model output.
P-value for the environmental association term in the fitted model, recorded as the unadjusted statistical significance measure.
Multiple-testing-adjusted p-value for the association term, if correction was applied across tested environmental variables or comparisons.
Lower bound of the confidence interval for the effect estimate, reported from the final association model output.
Upper bound of the confidence interval for the effect estimate, reported from the final association model output.
Summary of model fit reported for the association results, such as R-squared, marginal R-squared, conditional R-squared, or an equivalent fit statistic.
Operational assessment of whether the association results are stable and suitable for interpretation and downstream reporting, recorded after model output generation.
